skill.name: documentation-and-adrs
skill.description: Guides architecture decision records, API documentation, README structure, changelog maintenance, and documentation for human and AI contributors.
skill.summary: Create durable architecture and project documentation that preserves decisions, context, and operating guidance.
skill.author: addyosmani

security_audit.summary: All 28 external-command detections are Markdown examples or inline command references in SKILL.md, not executable behavior. The environment-file and system-reconnaissance detections also point to documentation examples, and no prompt injection or data-exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: Static scanning interprets Markdown code examples and inline command references as executable shell activity.
remediation.suggestion: Keep command examples clearly fenced and consider scanner-aware metadata or documentation exclusions for SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: The README example copies .env.example to .env, which can be misread as sensitive environment-file handling.
remediation.suggestion: State that .env.example must contain placeholders only and instruct users to review the file before adding secrets.

content.value_statement: Teams lose context when important technical decisions remain in chat, code comments, or individual memory. This skill turns architectural reasoning, API guidance, project instructions, and release changes into structured documentation.
actual_capabilities: Create ADRs with context, decision, alternatives, consequences, status, and dates.
Match existing ADR locations, naming schemes, formats, and section headings.
Draft API documentation with parameters, return values, errors, and examples.
Structure READMEs with setup steps, commands, architecture, and contribution guidance.
Maintain changelogs and document project conventions for future engineers and AI agents.
limitations: It does not inspect a repository unless the surrounding agent provides repository context.
It does not execute commands, create files, or verify that documented commands work.
It cannot determine whether an architectural decision is correct without project-specific constraints.
Its examples are templates and require review for local standards, security, and accuracy.

use_cases.title: Record an architecture decision
use_cases.description: Create an ADR that compares options, explains trade-offs, records the selected approach, and preserves consequences for future maintainers.

use_cases.title: Document a public API
use_cases.description: Draft consistent API documentation covering inputs, outputs, errors, authentication expectations, and representative usage guidance.

use_cases.title: Improve project onboarding
use_cases.description: Build a practical README, changelog structure, and agent guidance so contributors can understand setup, architecture, conventions, and recent changes.
use_cases.target_user: Open-source maintainers and developer experience teams

prompt_templates.title: Draft a simple ADR
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a concise ADR for this decision: [decision]. Include context, selected approach, two alternatives, consequences, status, and date. Use clear headings.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: capture one decision with a standard structure.

prompt_templates.title: Match repository conventions
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the repository context I provide and identify its ADR location, file format, numbering pattern, and headings. Then draft an ADR for [decision] that follows those conventions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: align new documentation with an existing project.

prompt_templates.title: Document a public API
prompt_templates.prompt: Write documentation for this public API: [API details]. Cover parameters, return values, validation, authentication, errors, and one realistic example. State unknowns instead of inventing behavior.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: create accurate reference material from supplied API details.

prompt_templates.title: Build a documentation system
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a documentation update for [project]. Propose ADRs for durable decisions, README sections for onboarding, API reference coverage, changelog entries, agent guidance, and a verification checklist. Preserve existing conventions and identify missing evidence.
prompt_templates.scenario: Expert: coordinate documentation across a changing project.

output_examples.input: We chose PostgreSQL over SQLite and MongoDB for a multi-user task application.
output_examples.output: An ADR outline with status, context, relational data requirements, alternatives considered, the PostgreSQL decision, and operational consequences.

output_examples.input: Document a task creation endpoint that requires a title and returns an identifier.
output_examples.output: API reference guidance covering the request fields, validation errors, authentication expectations, response details, and a short usage example.

output_examples.input: Create onboarding documentation for a project with a development server and test suite.
output: A README structure covering project purpose, setup, commands, architecture, and contribution practices.
A verification checklist for setup instructions, API documentation, known gotchas, and current agent rules.

best_practices: Provide repository conventions and factual project context before requesting documentation.
Document the reasoning, constraints, alternatives, and consequences instead of restating implementation details.
Review every generated command, example, link, and security statement against the current project.
anti_patterns: Do not invent repository conventions, API behavior, commands, or architectural constraints.
Do not create duplicate ADR numbering schemes or replace established project formats without evidence.
Do not use documentation as a substitute for implementation, testing, access control, or operational validation.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates ADRs, API documentation, README structures, changelog guidance, and documentation plans for human and AI contributors.

faq.question: Can it find the correct ADR format?
faq.answer: Yes, when you provide repository context. It can identify existing locations, naming patterns, file formats, and section headings.

faq.question: Does it write files automatically?
faq.answer: No. It produces documentation content and recommendations. The surrounding agent must review and apply file changes.

faq.question: Can it validate API behavior?
faq.answer: No. It can organize supplied API facts, but it cannot test endpoints or confirm undocumented implementation behavior.

faq.question: Who benefits most from this skill?
faq.answer: Engineering leads, API maintainers, open-source maintainers, developer experience teams, and agents working in unfamiliar repositories.

faq.question: How should generated documentation be reviewed?
faq.answer: Check decisions, commands, links, examples, security claims, project conventions, and dates against the current repository before publishing.
